paras: The stoning of the Masonic Temple on Courtland Street was an attack on a Black Masonic lodge hall in Baltimore, Maryland, on election night, Tuesday, November 3, 1903, and the following morning, by a crowd the Baltimore Afro-American put at more than two hundred white men and boys. No one was reported injured, but the front of the three-story building was left with hardly a pane of glass. The Afro-American presented the attack as the fruit of the Democratic campaign against "Negro domination" and faulted the police for their slow response.

On election night a large bonfire was built at the corner of Pleasant and Courtland streets, fed with dry goods boxes and surrounded by boys and men, while residents watched from doorsteps and windows. It was the regular meeting night of Enterprise Lodge No. 3, F. & A. Masons, at the colored Masonic Temple nearby.

As lodge members walked to the Temple, stones were thrown at them, which they at first ignored as "the usual outburst after almost every election." About nine o'clock, while the lodge was at work, windows began to break, and the members stopped their meeting and went into the street, where they were met with "a volley of stones." The members then went after the crowd, which scattered; as they moved up the street more stones were thrown and "one or two pistol shots were fired," though no one was hit.

Several members went to the Central Police Station to demand protection, and after persistent effort a single policeman was sent back with them. According to the Afro-American, he refused to hurry, saying he was tired and did not "feel like being bothered," and by the time he arrived the crowd had largely dispersed. Between six and seven o'clock on Wednesday morning the attackers returned and smashed the front of the building, breaking the shutters and the door knob; about a barrel of bricks and stones was gathered up afterward.

Enterprise Lodge still elected its officers despite the interrupted meeting, and the Knights Templar of St. Andrew's Grand Commandery held their annual conclave at the Temple on Wednesday night. On Wednesday William E. Tilghman, Grand Master of the state's colored Masons, set out for the Marshal's office about the attack, but was himself arrested on a streetcar on a conductor's word. The editorial said the building's owners would make every effort "to capture and lynch the offenders," as the text is printed; no report of an arrest of the attackers was found.

The only coverage found is in the Baltimore Afro-American of November 7, which ran the story on its front page under the headline "IS THIS WHAT WE ARE TO GET UNDER THE NEW DEMOCRATIC ADMINISTRATION?" and a deck reporting "Shouts of Nigger" and a policeman "In No Burry." Its editorial, "A Taste of Mob Violence," called the attack one of the most "dastardly outrages" in the city's memory and noted that earlier elections had seen Black voters driven from the polls, beaten and shot, but not the destruction of property. The paper laid the blame on "the speakers for the democratic ticket," and a week later cited the attack among post-election "outrages upon respectable colored citizens all over the city." No account of the attack in a white newspaper was found.

The news report places the first window-breaking at about nine o'clock with the lodge already in session, while the editorial says members were stoned on arrival and the building was being stoned "an hour after"; the two versions are compatible.

reader.title: Stoning of the Masonic Temple on Courtland Street, Baltimore
bases: A crowd of white men and boys stoned a Black Masonic lodge building and the members meeting in it, then returned the next morning to smash its front (A1, A2, A3).
All coverage comes from the Baltimore Afro-American (a front-page report, an editorial and two passing mentions in A1-A5); no other paper's account was found.

accounts.label: Afro-American news report
accounts.gist: A bonfire crowd first threw stones at arriving lodge members, then about nine o'clock broke the Temple's windows while the lodge met; members who came out were met with stones, chased the crowd, and one or two pistol shots were fired; the front was smashed again Wednesday morning.

accounts.label: Afro-American editorial
accounts.gist: Enterprise Lodge No. 3 members were stoned as they arrived, the building was stoned an hour later, and the attackers returned Wednesday morning to finish the destruction; the police were indifferent.

framing.detail: Headline 'IS THIS WHAT WE ARE TO GET UNDER THE NEW DEMOCRATIC ADMINISTRATION?' and editorial 'A Taste of Mob Violence' call it a 'dastardly' outrage bred by the Democrats' 'Negro domination' campaign and fault the police.

versions.value: Stones thrown at arriving members; about nine o'clock windows broken while the lodge was at work
Members stoned as they neared the building; 'an hour after' the building was being stoned

conflicts.note: Both from the same paper; the difference is minor and the accounts are compatible.

record_check.record: On a Wednesday morning ... a mob smashed ... Earlier that night a white mob of about two hundred had stoned the building
record_check.dossier: Order is reversed: the stoning began Tuesday night (election night) while Enterprise Lodge No. 3 met; the Wednesday 6-7 a.m. attack came after. The building was a Masonic Temple on Courtland Street.
White boys and men, 'upwards of two hundred', unnamed
Black (colored Masonic lodge members and their Temple)
Stoning and property damage are well supported; 'shooting' rests on 'one or two pistol shots' of unstated origin and target, with no one hit
Single source: one Black weekly (four items in one issue plus a passing mention a week later); no white-press coverage found

info: Tuesday night, with a second attack on Wednesday morning between six and seven o'clock (the paper of Saturday, November 7, 1903, refers to 'last Tuesday night', i.e. November 3-4, election night)
Colored Masonic Temple, Courtland Street, Baltimore; the crowd gathered around a bonfire at Pleasant and Courtland streets
Members of Enterprise Lodge No. 3, F. & A. Masons, meeting at the Temple, and the Temple building itself; no one named and no one reported hurt
A 'howling mob' of white boys and men; no one named

sources.note: Front-page report: a white crowd of 'upwards of two hundred' around an election-night bonfire stoned the colored Masonic Temple on Courtland Street; one or two pistol shots, no one hurt.
quotes: they made for the howling mob of upwards of two hundred white men and boys
more stones were thrown and one or two pistol shots were fired. Happily no one was injured by them.

sources.note: Continuation: members sought protection at the Central Police Station; one reluctant policeman sent; front of the building smashed again Wednesday morning.
quotes: "I have been on my feet all day and I am tired, and don't feel like being bothered."

sources.note: Editorial 'A Taste of Mob Violence': Enterprise Lodge No. 3 members stoned on arrival; police indifference; blames Democratic campaign speakers.
quotes: Tue whole thing was the outcome of the bitter partisan attack for political purposes by the speakers for the democratic ticket.
One of the worse features of the matter was the utter indifference of the police department

sources.note: Lodge column: Enterprise Lodge No. 3's meeting was 'interruped by the stoning of the Masonic Temple on last Tuesday night'; Knights Templar met at the Temple Wednesday night.
Arrest of Grand Master William E. Tilghman on a streetcar while on his way to the Marshal's office about 'the outrage upon the Masonic Temple'.
